task: Draft a help article explaining what sync conflicts are in the fictional sync application, why they occur, and how to resolve them using the three available actions. Include guidance on choosing between the actions, what happens to the discarded version, and what version information is shown in the dialog to aid the decision. Do not add a preview capability or automatic resolution not in the facts. Target 350–500 words.

facts.text: A conflict occurs when the same file is edited on two different devices between syncs.
The conflict dialog appears automatically when the sync service detects an unresolvable conflict.
The dialog shows the file name and the last-modified time of each version to help the user decide.
Keep this version retains the current device's version and discards the other device's version.
Keep other version retains the other device's version and discards the current device's version.
Save both as copies keeps both versions in the same folder, appending the device name and a timestamp to disambiguate the filenames.
The user cannot preview the content of either version from within the conflict dialog.
The discarded version is not recoverable after a choice is made.
Conflicts cannot be resolved automatically; the user must make a choice.
A common scenario that causes conflicts: editing a file offline on one device, then syncing while a second device has also changed the same file.
Save both as copies is appropriate when the user is unsure which version to keep and wants to compare content manually after closing the dialog.

forbidden_additions: A preview action available within the conflict dialog.
An invented recovery route for the discarded version.
preserve: What a conflict is and the common offline-edit scenario.
All three actions with their consequences.
File name and last-modified time as the decision aids.
No in-dialog preview; manual comparison after Save both as copies.
